value.account:
CHANGED
- New `orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py`: `ResumeScopePath`, `audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path)`, `ResumeProjectionIntegrityError`, `resolve_reached_call`, diagnostics with the twelve reasons and fixed context keys. Pure: reads only bundle+state, never mutates. Retry lineage lives in `resume_retry_lineage.py` (`index_retry_lineage`, `next_unused_retry_frame_id`, re-exported from the integrity module); loop bookkeeping rules in `resume_loop_progress.py`.
- `state_projection.py`: `enumerate_resume_slots`, `resolve_resume_step_id`, `resolve_call_boundary` (instance methods; the auditor uses an internal lookup so the public method is called once per reached call), `ResumeProjectionValidationError`, `CallBoundaryProjection.import_alias`; lowering fills the alias. Repeat-until maximums are carried in a new `WorkflowStateProjection.repeat_until_max_iterations` mapping, not on `IterationStepKeyProjection`, so the characterization goldens only gain `import_alias`.
- `StateManager.record_workflow_checksum_mismatch` / `record_resume_projection_integrity_failure`: rewrite only `status`, `error`, `updated_at` directly on the JSON file (RunState.from_dict would drop unknown root fields).
- CLI `resume`: observability override persistence moved after the checksum precheck and `audit_scope`; failure exits 1, prints message/field/offending value, persists only the envelope. Session close is wrapped so a failing close cannot replace the diagnostic.
- `WorkflowExecutor.execute(resume=True)`: structural-root guard (checksum recheck through `calculate_checksum`, then `audit_scope`) before the prologue; child call-frame executors skip it. `_handle_control_flow` returns `_stop` for a sticky error (also when nested in a loop result or for_each rows) and promotes it unchanged to `state['error']`; for_each stops at the failing iteration; finalization failures are supplemental (`failure.error` is the cleanup's own projection error or null) and never replace the run diagnostic.
- `CallExecutor`: frame selection by lineage, never mapping order; completed-frame id collision check before lineage grouping; after the ordinary validations a reached call resolves the boundary once, checks alias/lineage, checksum-validates and audits failed predecessors in ordinal order, then audits the running member, all before any child frame/state/executor exists. Failures become the caller's failed step result; a child's projection error is returned unwrapped (never `call_failed`). `_is_workflow_lisp_target` now checks `provenance.frontend_kind`.
- Workflow Lisp provenance: `_validate_one_lowered_workflow` stamps `frontend_kind="workflow_lisp"` on every compiler bundle; `build_frontend_bundle` no longer overwrites it. Default-resume route detection additionally requires `frontend_build_root`, so directly compiled bundles keep the old step-granular behavior.
- Classic YAML: `loader_import_aliases.py` composes the YAML node graph and reports duplicate aliases / duplicate top-level `imports` sections with `line L, column C` before bundle construction.
- Observability: `current_step_is_forensic` (failed run + sticky/checksum error) makes snapshots show the step `pending`, and removes it from heartbeat/cursor interpretation.
- Docs: `specs/state.md` section and `specs/acceptance/index.md` entries. Tests: new `tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py` (59 tests) plus updated existing tests.

DECISIONS / ALTERNATIVES
- Unknown vs unclaimed vs mismatch: id absent -> `unknown_explicit_step_id`; id exists and row name owned elsewhere -> `presentation_slot_mismatch`; id exists but row name not owned by the scope -> `unclaimed_explicit_step_row`. The spec's wording allows more than one reading; this was my interpretation.
- Rejected: patching `frame_id_with_overrides` to filter candidates (still mapping-order), and putting `max_iterations` on `IterationStepKeyProjection` (churns goldens).
- Several existing tests encoded the old behavior and were changed deliberately: legacy states lacking `current_step.step_id`, stub bundles without a projection (audit stubbed in 3 CLI tests, real bundle in one), characterization tests of the old gaps (rewritten to assert fail-closed), synthetic Lisp restore states that dropped a loop frame row but kept terminal bookkeeping (now invalid), a direct-executor adjudication test that rewrote the workflow source (now hits the checksum guard), and two golden files gaining `import_alias`.

NOT COVERED / UNCERTAIN
- `expected_owner.workflow_file` is the bundle's `provenance.workflow_path` (absolute), since the auditor may not know the workspace; a relative form may be expected.
- Full-suite comparison against a clean `git archive` baseline: no new failures; 49 failures are pre-existing, and `test_deadline_expiring_during_promotion_starts_no_terminal_ledger` is flaky on baseline too.
- Nested-loop rows are not separately persisted, so I only verified a completed nested for_each/repeat_until run audits clean; deeper nested-loop candidate enumeration is untested. No end-to-end `orchestrator resume` smoke run via the real CLI process was done beyond the updated in-process CLI tests. Not committed; docs/index and capability-matrix routing untouched.
value.summary: Resume now audits every persisted identity against the current projection (CLI root, executor root, each reached call) and fails closed with one sticky `resume_projection_integrity_error` before any mutation or effect; full suite shows no new failures versus baseline (49 pre-existing failures, one known-flaky adjudication timing test).
